title: The Story of Jack Frost
credits: Anna Matteo wrote this story for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: Now, from VOA Learning English, it's time for Words and Their Stories.
sentences.zh: 现在，来自美国之音英语学习，到了"词汇及其故事"的时间。

sentences.en: If this is your first time with us, this program explores words and expressions commonly used in American English.
sentences.zh: 如果这是你第一次加入我们，本节目将探讨英语中常用的词汇和表达。

sentences.en: We take a look at where they come from and how best to use them.
sentences.zh: 我们会看看它们从何而来，以及如何最好地使用它们。

sentences.en: So, as winter officially comes to half the world, today we celebrate an expression that means winter is coming.
sentences.zh: 所以，随着冬季正式降临地球的一半，今天我们庆祝一个表示冬季即将到来的表达。

sentences.en: When temperatures drop and a cold snap comes, that means one thing: Jack Frost has arrived!
sentences.zh: 当气温下降、寒流来袭时，这意味着一件事：霜先生来了！

sentences.en: Jack Frost represents the coming of dark, cold days.
sentences.zh: 霜先生代表着黑暗寒冷日子的到来。

sentences.en: He is the personification of winter, a human form of winter weather.
sentences.zh: 他是冬季的拟人化，是冬季天气的人类形态。

sentences.en: So, when we say, “Jack Frost is nipping at your nose,” we mean that you feel the cold, icy effects of winter on your face.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我们说"霜先生正在啃你的鼻子"时，我们的意思是你在脸上感受到了冬季冰冷刺骨的效果。

sentences.en: When a frost or deep freeze comes, you had better bundle up!
sentences.zh: 当霜冻或严寒来临时，你最好裹得严严实实！

sentences.en: You should wear enough clothing to stay warm.
sentences.zh: 你应该穿上足够的衣物以保持温暖。

sentences.en: Now, Jack Frost does, indeed, bring the cold of winter.
sentences.zh: 现在，霜先生确实带来了冬季的寒冷。

sentences.en: But he can also create beauty in nature.
sentences.zh: 但他也能在大自然中创造美丽。

sentences.en: Some traditions claim that Jack Frost is responsible for leaving ice and snow on windows, trees, the ground…anywhere it will stick.
sentences.zh: 一些传统声称，霜先生负责在窗户、树木、地面……任何能够附着的地方留下冰雪。

sentences.en: While we know frost is a natural event, it is fun to think that an imaginary creature named Jack Frost (or another name in some other cultures) changed the world into a winter wonderland!
sentences.zh: 虽然我们知道霜是一种自然现象，但想象一个名叫霜先生（在其他一些文化中另有其名）的虚构生物把世界变成了冬季仙境，这确实很有趣！

sentences.en: That is what poet Hannah Flagg Gould (1789-1865) must have been thinking when she wrote a poem called The Frost.
sentences.zh: 这正是诗人汉娜·弗拉格·古尔德（1789-1865）在写一首名为《霜》的诗歌时一定在想的事情。

sentences.en: Here are parts of that poem.
sentences.zh: 以下是那首诗的部分内容。

sentences.en: THE FROST looked forth, one still, clear night,
sentences.zh: 《霜》向四周望去，在一个宁静、清澈的夜晚，

sentences.en: And he said, “Now I shall be out of sight; ...
sentences.zh: 他说："现在我将会隐入视线之外；……

sentences.en: Then he went to the mountain, and powdered its crest,
sentences.zh: 然后他来到山边，给山巅撒上一层粉末，

sentences.en: He climbed up the trees, and their boughs he dressed
sentences.zh: 他爬上树木，为树枝盛装打扮

sentences.en: With diamonds and pearls…
sentences.zh: 钻石和珍珠……

sentences.en: With all of its beauty and extremes, winter is a great subject for songs and poetry.
sentences.zh: 冬天拥有所有的美丽与极端，是歌曲和诗歌的绝佳题材。

sentences.en: But now, let’s listen to how we use these wintry expressions in conversation:
sentences.zh: 但现在，让我们来听听我们在对话中如何使用这些冬季表达：

sentences.en: It is freezing outside.
sentences.zh: 外面冷得要命。

sentences.en: This cold snap came out of nowhere!
sentences.zh: 这场寒潮来得太突然了！

sentences.en: I don’t care how cold it is.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎有多冷。

sentences.en: I'm going on a hot date!
sentences.zh: 我要去赴一个浪漫的约会！

sentences.en: Is that all you’re wearing?
sentences.zh: 你就穿这些出去？

sentences.en: You need to bundle up or Jack Frost will be nipping at more than your nose!
sentences.zh: 你得裹严实点，不然杰克·弗罗斯特可要咬的不只是你的鼻子了！

sentences.en: I’ll be fine.
sentences.zh: 我没事。

sentences.en: I’m wearing my new coat.
sentences.zh: 我穿着我的新外套。

sentences.en: That it is NOT a winter coat.
sentences.zh: 那根本不是件冬季外套。

sentences.en: I mean, it looks great, but it’s much too thin.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它看起来很棒，但实在太薄了。

sentences.en: You will catch a cold. I know.
sentences.zh: 你会感冒的。我知道。

sentences.en: You can wear my new down coat.
sentences.zh: 你可以穿我的新羽绒服。

sentences.en: It keeps you warm up to minus 30 degrees Celsius!
sentences.zh: 它能让你保暖到零下30度！

sentences.en: I’m going on a date...not exploring the Arctic Circle! Thanks.
sentences.zh: 我是去约会……又不是去北极圈探险！谢谢。

sentences.en: But I am not wearing that big, thick black coat.
sentences.zh: 但我绝不会穿那件又大又厚的黑色外套。

sentences.en: Besides, the taxi will take me from door-to-door.
sentences.zh: 而且，出租车会直接把我送到门口。

sentences.en: But what if something goes wrong?
sentences.zh: 但如果出了什么意外怎么办？

sentences.en: What if the car skids on the ice and is involved in an accident?
sentences.zh: 如果车在冰上打滑出了事故怎么办?

sentences.en: You’ll have to walk to the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 你得走路去餐厅。

sentences.en: You might freeze to death!
sentences.zh: 你可能会冻死!

sentences.en: No, I won’t.
sentences.zh: 不,我不会去的。

sentences.en: I’ll just call an Uber to come and get me.
sentences.zh: 我就叫一辆Uber来接我。

sentences.en: And what if that vehicle runs out of fuel?
sentences.zh: 那如果那辆车没油了怎么办?

sentences.en: Then you’ll have to walk to get more.
sentences.zh: 那你就得走去加油。

sentences.en: No, the Uber driver will.
sentences.zh: 不,Uber司机会的。

sentences.en: I’ll just call another car.
sentences.zh: 我就再叫一辆车。

sentences.en: What if that new Uber driver is a pregnant woman and she goes into labor?
sentences.zh: 那如果那辆新的Uber司机是个孕妇,而且她要分娩了怎么办?

sentences.en: You’ll have to help.
sentences.zh: 你就得去帮忙。

sentences.en: You’ll have to wait outside in the cold until help arrives!
sentences.zh: 你就得在冷外面等到救援到来!

sentences.en: And the roads are already covered with five centimeters of snow!
sentences.zh: 而且路上已经铺了五厘米厚的雪了!

sentences.en: It could take the ambulance an hour to get to you!
sentences.zh: 救护车可能要一个小时才能到你那里!

sentences.en: If you’re wearing that thin coat…you’ll catch your death!!
sentences.zh: 如果你穿着那么薄的外套……你会冻出病的!!

sentences.en: The EMTs will find you frozen solid like a block of ice!!
sentences.zh: 急救人员会发现你冻得像冰块一样硬!!

sentences.en: Stop! Stop!! You win!
sentences.zh: 住手!住手!!你赢了!

sentences.en: Give me your coat!
sentences.zh: 把你的外套给我!

sentences.en: Good decision.
sentences.zh: 好决定。

sentences.en: Here’s my ride …
sentences.zh: 这是我的车……

sentences.en: Don’t forget gloves…a hat…and a scarf!
sentences.zh: 别忘了戴手套……戴帽子……还要系上围巾！

sentences.en: Okay, good bye. Have fun!
sentences.zh: 好的，再见。玩得开心！

sentences.en: And that’s the end of this Words and Their Stories.
sentences.zh: 这就是本期“Words and Their Stories”的全部内容。

sentences.en: Until next time!
sentences.zh: 我们下期再见！

glossary.def: a brief period of very cold weather
to injure or make numb with cold
to shake slightly (as from cold or fear)
an imaginary place of delicate beauty or magical charm
to sprinkle or cover with or as if with fine particles of something
to fail to grip the roadway
a vehicle equipped for transporting the injured or sick
a person who is trained to provide emergency medical services to patients who are being taken to a hospital : short for Emergency Medical Technician
